feedback.title: Record workflow feedback
feedback.imperative: Before committing, reflect honestly on how this run actually went: how closely you followed the skills, handoffs, and checklists; where you had to improvise or work around the instructions; what was ambiguous, missing, or contradictory; and what would have helped. Include the crew Workflow Feedback harvested at each gN-integrate. A 'none' answer requires a run-specific reason ('none — confirmed after review: <what you checked>'); bare 'none' entries fail the invariant check. Append one dated entry for this work-id to .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md (create it from templates/AGENT_FEEDBACK.template.md if absent — prefer the project copy under .agent-work/templates/, fall back to the bundled workbench template). This log persists across runs and is never archived with the work-id. Adjudicate each lesson before banking it — the playbook holds open problems you are carrying forward, not a log of everything learned. If a lesson is understood and fixable now, APPLY it this run (make the bounded edit, record it in AGENT_FEEDBACK) and do not add a playbook entry at all; a lesson goes in the bank (an add) ONLY because it needs to be re-observed to be understood, and every add must carry a bank_reason saying what re-observation will clarify. Applying to project doctrine (a docs/agents/* delta or a template working copy — any .md / .template.*) is a human call: it needs authority=human on the apply op, and in delegated/autonomous mode you do NOT self-apply doctrine — surface it to your principal (who may rule 'apply', or 'wait, observe it again') and defer with 'needs human' until they do. Applying a code target (with its test suite as proof) stays autonomous. Then distill what remains into the playbook: write structured delta ops (add [with bank_reason]/confirm/disconfirm/mention/retire/apply/defer — every add/confirm/disconfirm cites a grounding artifact line; corroborate with engine telemetry like rework counts, BLOCK verdicts, waives where possible) to .agent-work/301/lessons-delta.json with tick=true, and apply deterministically: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-301/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py .agent-work/301/lessons-delta.json --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md. Never edit LESSONS.md directly; if there are no lesson candidates, still apply a tick-only delta. Then settle every threshold-ripe lesson (python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-301/scripts/apply_lessons_delta.py --ripe --file .agent-work/LESSONS.md): for each, APPLY it (make the bounded edit to its target — a thin docs/agents/* delta or a project template working copy — confirmed by the human, then an apply op deletes it as paid), or for a constellation lesson EXPORT it (append to .agent-work/CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md — carry the originating lesson id in that entry's Lesson field so the upstream sweep groups recurrences on stable identity, rewording a recurring finding via amend not a new slug — then an export op marks it exported and pinned), or RESOLVE it if you can confirm the upstream fix has already shipped (a resolve op citing the shipping PR/commit marks the constellation lesson fixed-upstream: no longer ripe, immune to re-confirmation, and it ages out of the playbook — this is how an already-fixed defect stops being re-exported every run), or DEFER it with a reason (a broad or contradictory doctrine shift routes to a Charter refresh; an autonomous run without that latitude defers 'needs human'). Lessons flagged charter-review go to a Charter refresh. Then run the feedback invariant check before advancing: python C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/298-301/scripts/verify_agent_feedback.py 301 --phase feedback.

archive.title: Archive, commit, and push
archive.imperative: Commit all remaining work, including the appended .agent-work/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md entry — where the repo tracks .agent-work/. Push the branch to remote. When you open a PR on Windows, write the body to a temp file and use gh pr create -F <file> — a bash heredoc and a PowerShell @'...'@ here-string both fail for gh pr create --body (here-strings work for git commit -m, not PR bodies). Move .agent-work/301/ to .agent-work/archive/<date>-301/, leaving the unified AGENT_FEEDBACK.md at the agent-work root. The engine mechanically refuses closeout (c4) when the staged diff includes suspicious artifacts (oversized files, generated record dumps, disallowed dirs, binary/blob additions, large data files); if any are intentional, a human waives c4 via <engine> waive archive --cond c4 --authority human --reason "..." rather than hand-editing the spine. Release the engine session lease only as your VERY LAST action, AFTER the archive postconditions pass and you have run the engine's final advance on archive (the advance that marks the spine done): <engine> release --session-id commander-301. Release must come after that closing advance, never before it — the lease must cover every journaled action, so the release is the final journal entry; releasing earlier leaves archive's own closeout entries (attest/waive/advance) after the lease release and fails the terminal provenance check.

why_trail.why: Repo is the constellation-skills source: no docs/agents overlay, no architecture packet map; doctrine substituted from repo _shared references and design docs. Grep-before-plan confirms zero prior art for episode/stratum/rhyme, so the mission is a genuine build, not an honest-null. Prior art for the successor's neighbor is apply_lessons_delta.py: Markdown records under '### lesson:<slug>' headings with '- field: value' lines and append-only history, mutated ONLY through a validated all-or-nothing JSON delta script - that deterministic-mutation pattern is the shape the episode store should rhyme with.

Ask reconciled against the frozen order; scope fenced (in: record schema, Markdown-in-git store, deterministic retrieval, partition, retirement policy, Stratum A mapping, adversarial tests; out: capture wiring #305, consolidation #308, manifest #300, live LESSONS.md). Governing tension: the store must be deterministically findable while rhyme-detection stays a stochastic sensor job downstream, so the store exposes mechanical surface (stable ids, enumerable fields, exact-match retrieval) and never guesses. Obligation on #300's manifest stated as an obligation, not a design: enumerable (loaded-artifact-id, canonical-revision) pairs.

Plan frozen: 3 crew gates over a doc-first sequence so the record grammar is contractual before code builds against it. Two cold critics materially changed both the design recommendation and the gate plan - the design comparison had manufactured consensus on 2 of 6 claims (verified, corrected, Admiral told), and the gate plan had no exercised test for the priority-1 non-foreclosure obligation (now g2 c6 + g3 c7). Execution is deliberately BLOCKED at e0-context p1 pending the Admiral's convergence ruling.

Four gates driven to completion and merged. The design's central bet paid off: because every mechanism touching the held human decision routed through a named seam, binding the ratified answer at g4 changed adapter bodies and never a retrieval primitive.

Structural record reconciled directly, absent a packet map. The one repo-wide doc the change touches was filed to #308 rather than patched, because its correct wording depends on a ruling that issue owns - folding a cross-issue obligation onto the issue rather than carrying it.

Five findings filed, two fixed now, none banked worktree-locally. The launch order's pre-clearance made direct filing the default, which is what let findings like the autocrlf hazard reach #308 rather than dying in a verdict nobody re-reads.

Run accepted against the issue's four stated acceptance criteria, all met and evidenced, with the design-it-twice convergence ratified by the human rather than by me. Scope stated honestly: no episode has ever been captured (that is #305) and no consolidation has run (#308), so nothing here is evidence about a populated store.

Fenced-closeout path, not a waiver. The launch order fences the main checkout read-only, so the durable LESSONS.md/AGENT_FEEDBACK.md write is impossible; per commander doctrine the compliant substitute is the worktree-local staged trio plus a FENCE.md citing the order, which verify_agent_feedback.py accepts in lieu of the durable-root write - it passes at exit 0. Staged at .agent-work/staged-feedback/301/: AGENT_FEEDBACK.md, lessons-delta.json (12 ops - 2 confirms, 10 adds, 3 constellation-scoped), CONSTELLATION_FEEDBACK.md, FENCE.md. The delta was DRY-RUN against the real playbook rather than assumed valid, which caught two things I would otherwise have handed over broken: delta ops take task_class/bank_reason with underscores while the rendered playbook field uses hyphens, and I had authored the rendered form throughout; and the playbook is at 16 active against a cap of 20, so only 4 of my 10 adds can land. I supplied my own cap-drop ordering with reasons into FENCE.md where the harvester reads, rather than leaving the judgment to someone without the run context - keeping a-panel-inherits first because #300's op lands as a confirm against that id and dropping it would fork the identity the Admiral ruled to preserve. I also dropped a redundant confirm I had authored against a lesson added in the same delta.

Issue #301 closed end to end. The store the epic asked for exists as Markdown in git at a tracked path, its partition is enforced rather than documented, its retirement policy is bound to the layout the human ratified, and a seeded episode is retrievable across a real process boundary and a real git worktree boundary. PR #320 merged. What the run is actually evidence for is narrower and more interesting than the deliverable: five independent cold reads each found a real defect the prior gate's own tests could not see, and every one was a silent wrong answer rather than a crash.
